questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I visited Edinburgh when I was fourteen and I knew then that I wanted to come back to live there. The exchange programme was an excellent opportunity to do just that.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I though a semester abroad was over-hyped, but it was truly an intense and amazing learning experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easily. The university has an excellent system, and are very good at informing students. As long as you keep up with your school e-mail, you're good to go.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not applicable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: No additional comments.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are a couple different options for student accomodation through the host university, I stayed in Pollock Halls. I got the offer through calling the university accomodation team.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Fully catered breakfast and dinner included in rent. There was also a pantry on each floor.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It might be more expensive than you would think, double check what the cost is for one semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was happy with my room, the food was sub-par. The best thing about it was the fact that you ate dinner with your friends every day and it was easy to make spontaneous plans. Sometimes we would just watch a movie in one of the common rooms.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very easy and well-organized.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to do an immigration check, where they checked a potential visa (not applicable for me), passport and that I was correctly enrolled.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Easily available advice place and accesible staff at the university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful, I got enrolled in all four classes I applied for originally.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about it too much, as long as you keep up with your e-mail it is very easy and they are very available to help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All professors displayed an exstensive knowledge of their fields.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Third-year BA courses, on the same level as I would have taken in my home institution.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar, but with much more written work, which was a welcome change.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Critical Practice: Criticism
Critical Practice: Poetry
Modernism and Empire
Scottish Emigrant Traditions

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Pick what sounds interesting. From personal experience, I would recommend Modernism and Empire.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Rent was more expensive than I expected. You'll want to save up for fun activities too, to not miss out.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent was more expensive than expected. I didn't travel as much.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a wide variety of things to do.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many many different types of sports and clubs. Diving, archery, normal sports, film club, Taylor Swift club etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely the Bad Film Club. Hold a screening of a bad film every monday, the newsletters are always hilarious.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Walk around! There is so much to see in Edinburgh. Take a day trip to St. Andrews.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, I feel at home in Edinburgh.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I talked almost exclusively with othe rexchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It is slightly more diverse than Denmark, which is, to me, always a liberating feeling and environment.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have fun, save up, don't stress about the academic aspects too much, you're not there to sit in your room for ten hours a day.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use all their resources. They want to help but you have to initiate contact.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Going abroad and meeting new people. Changing my environment to a place where no one knows me and I can be the newest version of myself.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being far away from family and friends from back home during hard times.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO! You won't regret it

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
